title: Why Heat Pumps are Immensely Important Right Now
summary: An explainer argues cold-climate air-source heat pumps now beat on-site gas burning on energy for nearly all of a Chicago winter, while noting cost comparisons are local.

assertions.quote: they have coefficients of performance that are greater than 1.
it actually makes more sense to burn natural gas in a power plant to generate electricity than it does to pipe that gas into homes

verdicts.note: With about 40-50% plant efficiency, a seasonal COP above roughly 2-2.5 beats a condensing furnace, which most modern units achieve except in deep cold.

RMI's water-heating example finds a heat pump water heater powered by a combined-cycle gas plant burns less gas and emits less than a gas-fired water heater, so burning gas at the plant is more efficient than burning it at home.

assertions.quote: will reduce the total amount of fuel required to heat your home over a year — even with today’s electric grid.
the cost of electricity in your area compared to that of natural gas makes cost comparisons a hyper-local exercise
Many units now guarantee operation down to -13°F which is -25°C
but they won’t attain their full output and will have a poor COP at that temp
Still generally better than 1, though, so it still makes sense

verdicts.note: Cold-climate models keep COP above 1 down to about -13°F, but older or standard units approach COP 1 in deep cold.

assertions.quote: But we are definitely one of those places where the conventional wisdom says heat pumps don’t work.
The thing to keep in mind about these backups, though, is that they are needed only in exceptional cases.

verdicts.note: Field studies in cold climates show backup covering a small share of heat, but more in very cold places or with poor controls.
